meta.reviewer: Claude (Opus 5) via Claude Code weekly review
meta.coverage: Top 15 by analystScore plus sticky accumulate holdovers (AMZN, TSM, JBL) and Core-tier pass entries kept under review (MTSI, POET, TSLA), with AMD and GFS retained from the 1 September roster. MU initiated: it had carried an open position in the calls ledger since 17 August with no verdict behind it. AMKR removed, having fallen out of Core tier. Written 15 September with /pre-review run the same day, so every verdict here carries independent seat research except MRVL, AMZN, TSM, COHR, AMD, GFS, POET, JBL and TSLA, which lost the pre-review cap and say so.
meta.disclaimer: Second-opinion research notes on @aleabitoreddit's ideas. Personal research tool — not investment advice.

focus.headline: Memory repriced. The market sold the news.
focus.dek: Server DRAM up 13–18% next quarter with Samsung asking 20%, MU's 16 LTAs and SNDK's Meta deal lock the demand in — and memory names sold off anyway. SNDK joins the book.

verdicts.view: Held at accumulate, and his read on demand is right. NVIDIA delivered $96.2bn with data centre at $89.0bn, guided Q3 to $108bn, and stated it assumes no data centre compute revenue from China at all. He is also right that the 70% growth figure is a supply statement rather than a demand one. What he has not connected is the cost side, and it is the same trade he is on the other end of. Gross margin is guided down to 74.0% from 75.0% delivered, the first sequential compression this cycle, while revenue guides up 12%. The memory squeeze he is long through Micron, SK hynix and Sandisk arrives here as margin. Both legs of his book cannot win the same dollar.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 28 Aug entry at $217.13. No add at the current level; add below $195, which is where the one-notch margin step is paid for. Size this as the funding leg of the book, not the growth leg.
verdicts.changesMind: Gross margin guided below 72%, which would make memory cost structural rather than a quarter of mix. On the other side, China data centre compute re-entering the outlook is upside nobody is carrying.

verdicts.view: Held at wait, and this week the desk was wrong before he was. Its own pre-review finding asserted the 100 million laser figure had never been disclosed. It had: a 3 September release commits USD 30m to Glasgow for capacity above 100 million CW DFB lasers annually, operational Q4 2027. That finding has been retracted and replaced in the feed. So the number is real, dated and company-stated, which is the strongest evidence this thesis has ever had. What has not changed is everything between here and Q4 2027. Q2 net sales fell 12% to SEK 53.8m, adjusted EBITDA worsened to SEK -35.5m, and the company placed 12,280,701 shares at SEK 57 on 1 July into an oversubscribed book. The shares are near half that price ten weeks later. Institutions bought this capacity story with better access than this desk has and are down by half.
verdicts.execution: No add. The SEK 57 placement price is the reference level, not the recent high, and the capacity date is five quarters out. If long, hold at reduced size. The thing to wait for is a customer commitment against the Glasgow capacity, not another capacity headline.
verdicts.changesMind: A named customer commitment or LTA against the Glasgow line moves this to accumulate. A further equity raise below SEK 57, or the Q4 2027 date slipping, moves it to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at wait, and the reason has changed from financing to revenue quality. The 10-Q shows the top three customers at 42%, 26% and 24% of second-quarter revenue, and Digicomm alone holding $211.0m of $314.0m in receivables. Receivables are 164% of quarterly revenue. The single largest exposure at a name the analyst files under AI photonics is a cable-television distributor, and the company is guiding Q3 to $255-290m against $191.9m delivered. Nothing in his feed touches this. He has the demand right, and Goldman's optical revision and the Citi laser note support it, but a company that is nearly doubling revenue while two thirds of its receivables sit with one CATV counterparty is carrying a risk that does not appear in any of his posts.
verdicts.execution: No new capital, unchanged. The level to watch is not the price but days sales outstanding. Wait for a quarter with no fresh equity issuance, 1.6T revenue actually recognised, and receivables falling as a share of sales.
verdicts.changesMind: A Digicomm receivable provision, or days sales outstanding above 180, moves this to pass. Receivables falling below one quarter of revenue with 1.6T recognised moves it to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Held at wait, and an upgrade to accumulate was drafted this week and then rejected. The case for it was strong: FY26 revenue $3,014.0m, up 83.2%, Q1 FY27 guided to $1.225-1.275bn, which reaches the $1.25bn target model more than a quarter early at a 39.5-40.5% operating margin; Broadcom's own chief executive saying EML and CW laser demand is far surpassing supply while Broadcom triples capacity; Goldman lifting the 2028 optical module TAM 115% to $148.5bn; and Lumentum the only photonics name on this roster up over the month. What stopped it was the desk's own falsifier, written nine days ago and not met. The 10 September memo set the accumulate condition as the conversion process clearing with the share count settling, and as of 14 August the company had received early conversion requests over $757.8m of principal with every series deep in the money. That process is still running. Upgrading a week after writing that condition, on no new capital-structure information, would make the falsifier decorative.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 12 Aug position at $820.59. No add until the next filing shows the conversion requests cleared and a settled diluted share count. That filing, not the price, is the trigger.
verdicts.changesMind: Conversion requests clearing with the share count settling moves this to accumulate immediately — the operating case is already made. Non-GAAP operating margin guided below 35%, or a further extinguishment charge with the count still moving, moves it to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at wait despite a 27.7% month, and the company's own release is the reason. Sandisk states that sequential growth came about one-third from volume and two-thirds from price. Gross margin is 84.6% against 26.2% a year earlier, and consumer revenue fell 32% sequentially, so the non-AI business is shrinking underneath the print. The board then authorised an additional $14bn buyback, funded from operating cash flow, at a price up twentyfold in a year and at a margin with no precedent. He cites the company expecting 80% gross margins to continue into 2030; that is a forecast about an ASP, not about a cost structure. Buying back stock with peak-cycle cash at peak-cycle prices is the allocation decision memory companies have made at every top.
verdicts.execution: The 21 Aug trim at $1,603.59 stands and no capital goes back in here. If the position is still on, let it run but do not add. A re-entry level worth writing down is below $1,050, which is roughly where the August dip traded.
verdicts.changesMind: Gross margin guided below 70% turns this to pass. Sustained volume-led rather than price-led growth, with consumer stabilising, would move it back to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Initiated at wait. This is a coverage gap being closed: the calls ledger has carried an open Micron position since 17 August with no verdict behind it, which should not have happened. His case is the strongest version of the memory argument and the numbers support it — fiscal Q3 revenue $41.5bn, up 346%, gross margin 84.9%, HBM4 for Vera Rubin shipping since March and ramping at roughly twice the pace of HBM3E 12-high. The desk's reservation is not the demand but what the margin is made of. At 84.9% going to a guided 86%, nearly all incremental revenue is price rather than volume, so the earnings base is a spot-price artefact and a single-digit ASP decline removes a disproportionate share of profit. SK hynix is meanwhile accelerating M15X and opening Yongin Phase 1 in early 2027, which is the supply response starting.
verdicts.execution: No add before 30 September. Micron has set its own bar at $50bn revenue and $31 EPS and the stock is below the 17 August entry at $971.66, so the asymmetry into the print is poor. Decide size after the print, not before it.
verdicts.changesMind: Gross margin guided below 75% at any point, or HBM pricing disclosed as contracted lower for 2027, turns this to pass. A 2027 HBM book locked at current pricing with capex discipline holding across Samsung and SK hynix moves it to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Held at wait, and as with Lumentum an upgrade was drafted and rejected. He read the after-hours selloff as an overreaction and the direction of that is right: AI semiconductor revenue was $16.7bn, up 221%, guided to $21.7bn, with $13.7bn of free cash flow in the quarter funding the ramp against $59.4bn of debt without touching equity. Down 18.1% in a month on a quarter that beat its own AI target by $700m. But the desk's 10 September memo set the accumulate condition as customer concentration falling as new programmes ramp, or a December quarter showing XPU bookings compounding behind more than one name — and with one distributor at roughly half of revenue and five end customers at 55%, neither has happened. This week's own research pointed the other way: non-GAAP gross margin fell to 74.9% from 78.4% and the CFO named the cause, that XPUs carry more memory content and dilute mix as they grow. Upgrading on a week whose new evidence was bearish would be incoherent.
verdicts.execution: No position yet, and the price is now doing the work the business has not. Below $310 the concentration risk starts being paid for; that is the level to act on if the December quarter brings breadth. Do not initiate on the drawdown alone.
verdicts.changesMind: Disclosed customer concentration falling, or December-quarter XPU bookings behind more than one name, moves this to accumulate. A named flagship programme moving to Marvell or MediaTek, or gross margin below 72%, moves it to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at wait after a 19.5% month, and the reservation is now dated rather than general. Q2 revenue was 79.3tn won at a 76% operating margin with an 69.4tn won net cash position, which is the least fragile way to own the squeeze and supports his case. But SK hynix's own release pairs capital discipline language with accelerating M15X mass production and a Yongin Phase 1 cleanroom opening in early 2027. Discipline is the wording; acceleration is the substance, and the 76% margin is what pays for the supply that ends it. He quotes KB Securities forecasting the tightest supply conditions in history for next year. That forecast and this capex plan cannot both be right past 2027. Note also that Q2 net profit of 93.9tn won exceeds operating profit of 60.5tn won, so a third of the headline sits below the operating line; underwrite the 60.5tn.
verdicts.execution: No new capital into a 19.5% month. The reason to own this rather than Micron is the balance sheet, so if the memory sleeve needs trimming, trim Micron and Sandisk first and keep this.
verdicts.changesMind: The Yongin early-2027 date being pulled forward again, or 2027 capex guided above this year's, turns this to pass. Capex held flat with DRAM contract pricing rising into 2027 moves it to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Downgrade from accumulate to wait, entirely on the desk's own reading of the filing. Alphabet raised $49.6bn of equity and mandatory convertible preferred in June, issued $20.3bn of senior unsecured notes in the quarter, and signed a $40bn at-the-market programme. Long-term debt went from $46.5bn to $98.2bn in six months. The company the analyst treats as a demand anchor, and holds personally, is now funding its buildout from capital markets rather than from operations. The reported earnings hide it: of $112.1bn in Q2 net income, $98.0bn is other income, chiefly unrealised gains on equity securities, against $40.8bn of operating income. The operating business is excellent — Cloud up 82% to $24.8bn with margin above 35% — and net property and equipment rose $74.6bn in six months, which is real capacity. None of that is the issue. The issue is that the equity is now financing the capex, and no post of his mentions it.
verdicts.execution: Step down to wait and stop adding. This is a financing-structure call, not a business call, so it is a sizing decision rather than an exit. Hold what is on. Restore accumulate on a quarter with positive free cash flow and no new issuance.
verdicts.changesMind: A quarter with free cash flow back above zero and no fresh equity or notes restores accumulate. Drawing on the $40bn ATM for anything other than employee tax obligations moves this to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at wait. The week gave him two genuine positives: the Palantir partnership naming Nebius its preferred sovereign AI infrastructure partner, and Oracle disclosing that renewed GPU capacity resold at a 20% premium on equipment four years and older, which is a direct hit on the rapid-depreciation bear case. Both are real. The desk's reservation is the financing shape underneath. First-half capital spending was $8,130.3m against $981.3m of revenue, an 8.3x ratio; debt is $8.55bn against $8.04bn of cash after an upsized $5.75bn convertible in August; and first-half net income of $430.8m from continuing operations includes a $780.6m equity revaluation gain, so the operating business lost money. The position is a bet on continued capital-market access, not on utilisation, and that is a different risk from the one he is describing.
verdicts.execution: No new capital after a 19% month. If owned, treat convertible issuance terms as the health metric rather than ARR growth, because that is what actually gates the build.
verdicts.changesMind: A convertible priced at a lower conversion premium than the August deal, or sequential ARR growth below 20%, turns this to pass. Positive free cash flow with the capex guide intact moves it to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Held at wait, and this is a coverage note as much as a call: Marvell lost the pre-review cap this week, so no independent research sits behind it and the desk is reading his posts alone. What those contain is genuinely useful — Marvell's SVP of optical engineering at Semicon Taiwan naming Europe and Japan as laser sourcing geographies, and putting near-packaged optics at late 2027 to 2028 with full co-packaged optics after. That timing is the same one MACOM gave, from a different company, which is the strongest cross-check available this week and it argues the CPO transition is a 2028 revenue event rather than a 2027 one. Up 7.1% in a month against SMH down 4.3%.
verdicts.execution: No capital until it survives a pre-review pass with independent numbers behind it. Nothing here should be acted on from his posts alone.
verdicts.changesMind: An ASIC socket loss at a named hyperscaler, or NPO timing moving out again past 2028. A dated first-generation CPO win with disclosed volumes moves this to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Held at accumulate. The Qualcomm agreement is the week's substantive item: warrants over roughly a $4bn stake tied to up to $60bn of milestone revenue from a custom-silicon partnership, on top of existing equity and warrant positions in Alchip, Marvell, Astera and AAOI. His framing that Amazon is becoming a semiconductor index is glib but directionally right, and it is the cheapest way this roster gets diversified exposure to the custom-silicon build. Down 8.2% in a month against SMH down 4.3%, with the capex-driven free-cash-flow headwind that Alphabet is also carrying — the difference being that Amazon has not yet had to issue equity against it.
verdicts.execution: Continue to accumulate on weakness. Add below $235. Watch the same financing line that moved Alphabet down this week: the moment capex is funded by issuance rather than operations, this steps to wait on the same reasoning.
verdicts.changesMind: An equity or large note issuance to fund capex, on Alphabet's pattern. A retail margin deterioration that removes the cash cushion underneath AWS would do it too.

verdicts.view: Held at wait, and the desk found the fact that explains the tape. AXT's $715.8m of cash and investments is issued equity, not retained earnings: 8,560,311 shares sold at $64.25 in April for roughly $550m, expressly to expand Beijing Tongmei's indium phosphide capacity. The shares now trade below that price. The capital raised to solve a Western shortage is being deployed inside the jurisdiction whose export permits decide whether the product can leave. The operating evidence remains the best in the book — Q2 revenue $47.6m at 44.9% gross margin with $11.1m of net income, against 8.0% gross margin a year earlier — and his thesis was validated externally this week by the Bloomberg piece naming indium phosphide substrates a key industry risk. Both things are true. The market is pricing the permit, not the margin.
verdicts.execution: The 1 Sep trim at $60.61 stands. No new capital until export permits show a routine cadence. The $64.25 April placement price is the reference level; buying below it is buying what institutions bought, which is not the same as buying cheaply.
verdicts.changesMind: Permits granted on a routine cadence with China falling as a share of revenue restores accumulate. A permit refusal, a delay disclosed as material, or a Tongmei redemption event moves this to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at accumulate. He restated the bull case this week and named TSMC among his five favourite megacaps, and the reasoning stands up: it is the one node everything on this roster passes through, it has demonstrated it can raise prices, and COUPE gives it the silicon-photonics integration step that the Marvell commentary places in Taiwan. Up 0.6% over a month while SMH fell 4.3% and the photonics names fell 16%, which is what a chokepoint looks like when the market is de-risking. The desk's reservation is only that TSM lost the pre-review cap this week, so this verdict carries no independent research.
verdicts.execution: Hold the 10 Aug position at $420.04. Add below $385. This is the position that should be sized to hold through a capex-cycle scare rather than traded around.
verdicts.changesMind: Intel 18A or Samsung SF2 winning a named leading-edge AI customer away. A capex guide cut, which would say TSMC does not believe the 2027 demand its customers are guiding to.

verdicts.view: Downgrade from accumulate to wait, on his own channel work rather than against it. He surfaced the Coherent transcript line that matters: Coherent was a major merchant laser supplier and has largely withdrawn, with management saying they do not see any time in the near future where they would sell indium phosphide lasers externally, and that over the long term some portion of datacom will be bought in. In a market he correctly describes as supply-constrained, that turns Coherent from a seller of the scarce input into a buyer of it. He reads this as bullish for the merchant suppliers, and it is. It is not bullish for Coherent's own cost line. Down 16.1% in a month, the second-worst on this roster after Sivers, which suggests the market has read the same transcript.
verdicts.execution: Trim the 21 Aug position at $289.67 rather than exit; the datacom franchise is intact and the stock is 3.1% higher on the week. No new capital. The merchant-laser exposure this position was partly held for now sits better in Lumentum.
verdicts.changesMind: Coherent re-entering the merchant laser market with disclosed external volumes restores accumulate. Gross margin compression attributed to bought-in laser cost moves this to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at wait. Up 5.8% in a month against SMH down 4.3%, and the only substantive item in his feed is that Situational Awareness bought AMD options — a positioning datapoint, not a thesis. AMD lost the pre-review cap this week so no independent numbers sit behind this call. The structural reservation is unchanged and is now sharper given what the desk found at NVIDIA and Broadcom: AMD buys the same HBM into a market where the memory vendors are earning 76% to 86% margins, without NVIDIA's pricing power or Broadcom's custom-silicon lock-in to absorb it.
verdicts.execution: No capital. If accelerator exposure is wanted, it is already held through NVIDIA at better terms.
verdicts.changesMind: A named hyperscaler committing to MI-series volumes at disclosed scale. Gross margin holding above 50% through the HBM cost step would also force a rethink.

verdicts.view: Held at pass, and the exit is being tested. The call was made on a product date — a 75mW CW laser still in high-temperature testing with production a potential late-2027 start and near-packaged optics revenue in 2028 — and that has not changed. What has is the rest of the company. MACOM delivered fiscal Q3 revenue of $342.2m, up 18.4% sequentially at 58.3% gross margin, with operating income at 22.5% of revenue against 14.9% a year earlier, and guided fiscal Q4 to $415-425m. That is a 21-24% sequential step, the steepest on this roster. The programme slipped; the company did not. The desk should be honest that it exited a compounding business over one product line, and that Marvell's own late-2027-to-2028 NPO timing this week says MACOM's date was industry-normal rather than a company-specific failure.
verdicts.execution: Stay out, but replace the product falsifier with a numeric one. Re-entry trigger: a fiscal Q4 print at or above $425m with data centre revenue still growing, which would say the exit was a thesis error rather than a timing one.
verdicts.changesMind: Fiscal Q4 revenue at or above $425m with data centre growth intact moves this back to wait. A dated first-generation CPO win with disclosed volumes moves it to accumulate.

verdicts.view: Held at wait. One mention this week, and it arrived inside his criticism of Sivers rather than as a GlobalFoundries thesis: his complaint was that Sivers talked about near-term revenue instead of the Ayar and GlobalFoundries silicon-photonics work and the H2 2027 to 2028 opportunity. That is the whole GFS case on this desk — it is the photonics foundry partner in a transition the rest of the roster now dates to 2028, not 2027. Down 11.5% in a month. Nothing in the week changes the shape: a mature-node foundry with an option on silicon photonics attached, where the option is the reason to hold it and the option is a year further out than it looked in August.
verdicts.execution: No capital. This is a 2028 story being asked to carry a 2026 valuation, and the pre-review cap has not reached it, so nothing independent supports a position.
verdicts.changesMind: A disclosed silicon-photonics production win with volumes, or Ayar reaching production on the GF platform with a named module customer. Mature-node utilisation falling further would move it to pass.

verdicts.view: Held at pass. Zero mentions since the last review and none at all since 30 August, which is the cleanest signal available: the analyst has stopped talking about it. Down 12.4% in a month. The position that took it to pass — an optical interposer story with no disclosed production revenue against merchant suppliers who are shipping — is unchanged, and the week's evidence made it worse rather than better, since Lumentum and Broadcom both described capacity expansions that fill the gap POET exists to fill.
verdicts.execution: Stay out. No re-entry level is worth writing down until there is disclosed revenue.
verdicts.changesMind: A production order with disclosed volumes and a named customer. Continued silence with no revenue eventually removes this from coverage altogether rather than changing the call.

verdicts.view: Held at accumulate as a sticky holdover — zero mentions since 30 August, so this verdict is carried on the existing thesis rather than refreshed by the week. That thesis is intact and is actually strengthened by what happened elsewhere: Jabil is the manufacturing partner named in the Sivers 1.6T LRO path, and the Glasgow capacity announcement on 3 September makes that path more concrete, not less. Down 9.8% in a month with the rest of photonics, on no company news this desk has captured. It is the lowest-beta way on this roster to hold the optical build.
verdicts.execution: Hold. Add below $270 if the photonics drawdown continues, since the Jabil position in the chain is contract manufacturing rather than merchant component supply and does not carry the equity-issuance risk that marked Sivers, AAOI and AXT this week.
verdicts.changesMind: Losing the Sivers or a comparable 1.6T programme. A guide-down in the intelligent infrastructure segment would move this to wait.

verdicts.view: Held at pass, for the same reason as always: this is a tiering artefact, not a conviction name. Its one mention this week was a joke about what retail investors hold. He has said he owns it personally and it appears in multi-ticker recap posts, which is exactly the mechanism that inflates mention counts without conviction behind them. Up 9.5% in a month on nothing this desk tracks. It has no place in an AI hardware supply chain book.
verdicts.execution: Stay out. This is a coverage-hygiene entry, not a position.
verdicts.changesMind: Nothing in the supply chain. If Dojo or AI5 silicon became a disclosed merchant business with external customers, it would be a different company and a new thesis.
